subject: plotting lines with a Date legend

messages.author: 12a8430c1bf3f70b
messages.subject: plotting lines with a Date legend
parts:
Good morning from sunny Dublin!

I'm trying to understand some ggplot2 behaviour with respect to dates.

library(ggplot2)
dfk <- structure(list(Date = structure(c(15425, 15426, 15427, 15428, 
15429, 15425, 15426, 15427, 15428, 15429, 15425, 15426, 15427, 
15428, 15429, 15425, 15426, 15427, 15428, 15429), class = "Date"), 
    Delta = c(7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 14, 14, 14, 14, 14, 21, 21, 21, 
    21, 21, 30.4, 30.4, 30.4, 30.4, 30.4), Rate = c(0, 0, 0, 
    0, 0, 0.023, 0.023, 0.022, 0.023, 0.022, 0.054, 0.053, 0.051, 
    0.052, 0.052, 0.109, 0.106, 0.103, 0.103, 0.103)), .Names = c("Date", 
"Delta", "Rate"), row.names = c(NA, 20L), class = "data.frame")

# this does not produce what I am looking for...
qplot(Delta, Rate, data=dfk, ylab='Rate', xlab='Days', colour=Date, geom='line')

# but this does - however I'll have to tidy up the name of the legend afterwards.
qplot(Delta, Rate, data=dfk, ylab='Rate', xlab='Days',
        colour=as.character(Date), geom='line')

Could somebody explain to me why this occurs please?  Is is a reasonable request that the second should occur by default - with a nicer legend too :-) ?

Is there a better way to get this effect?

Many thanks in advance,
Seán

On Sun, Apr 1, 2012 at 4:39 AM, Sean O'Riordain <sea...@acm.org> wrote:
> Good morning from sunny Dublin!
>
> I'm trying to understand some ggplot2 behaviour with respect to dates.
>
> library(ggplot2)
> dfk <- structure(list(Date = structure(c(15425, 15426, 15427, 15428,
> 15429, 15425, 15426, 15427, 15428, 15429, 15425, 15426, 15427,
> 15428, 15429, 15425, 15426, 15427, 15428, 15429), class = "Date"),
>     Delta = c(7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 14, 14, 14, 14, 14, 21, 21, 21,
>     21, 21, 30.4, 30.4, 30.4, 30.4, 30.4), Rate = c(0, 0, 0,
>     0, 0, 0.023, 0.023, 0.022, 0.023, 0.022, 0.054, 0.053, 0.051,
>     0.052, 0.052, 0.109, 0.106, 0.103, 0.103, 0.103)), .Names = c("Date",
> "Delta", "Rate"), row.names = c(NA, 20L), class = "data.frame")
>
> # this does not produce what I am looking for...
> qplot(Delta, Rate, data=dfk, ylab='Rate', xlab='Days', colour=Date,
> geom='line')
>
> # but this does - however I'll have to tidy up the name of the legend
> afterwards.
> qplot(Delta, Rate, data=dfk, ylab='Rate', xlab='Days',
>         colour=as.character(Date), geom='line')
>
> Could somebody explain to me why this occurs please?

Groups are set to the interaction of nominal variables. Since date is
not nominal, you need to either change it to a nominal variable or
specify grouping. For the second approach you can do

geom='line', group = Date)

Alternatively, you can change Date to a factor before plotting:

dfk$Date <- as.factor(dfk$Date)
qplot(Delta, Rate, data=dfk, ylab='Rate', xlab='Days', colour=Date, geom='line')

> request that the second should occur by default - with a nicer legend too
> :-) ?

Probably not. The current system uses reasonable defaults (i.e.,
groups set to interaction of factors), probably this should not be
changed.

>
> Is there a better way to get this effect?

Use one of the two methods demonstrated above.

Best,
Ista
